basis: Inflammation of the cerebrum; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not specified.
Defining vertebral and rib malformations, arthrogryposis and severe pulmonary hypoplasia.
Cleft lip and palate define the disease; lagophthalmos and lower-eyelid ectropion impair eyelid function in 2/2 patients.
Benign cutaneous epithelial neoplasm arising from the follicular sheath.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the jejunum.
Defining microcephaly and chorioretinal dysplasia, with developmental delay and visual impairment.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae, epiphyses and metaphyses; supplied phenotypes are skeletal.
Skin/nail disease, marrow failure and cellular immunodeficiency; oral leukoplakia 80-99%, GI stenosis 30-79%. Frequent neurologic, renal and skeletal abnormalities omitted by cap.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; hypermetropia 41/41, strabismus 24/76, atrial septal defect 16/23 and hearing impairment 38/119 support involvement.
Intellectual disability and developmental delay in 16/16, with common seizures and abnormalities of muscle tone; no independent muscle disease.
Structural skeletal myopathy with nemaline bodies and weakness; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung disease.
Retinal degeneration with congenital visual impairment and sensorineural hearing loss; both defining and present in 6/6 patients.
Laceration of the uterine broad ligament with cervical hypermobility; confined to reproductive structures.
Primary central nervous system glial tumour; MAPK alteration does not establish an endocrine or metabolic disorder.
Malignancy of the meninges; unusual extracranial child concepts do not define this umbrella.
Defining anemia, B-cell deficiency and developmental delay; renal tubular dysfunction 7/9, nephrocalcinosis 3/7. Retinal dystrophy 3/6, deafness 5/11 and lactic acidosis 3/4 omitted by cap.
Primary dystonia causes laryngeal and cervical motor dysfunction; dysphonia does not establish direct airway damage.
Congenital meningeal herniation through a defining cranial bone defect.
Bacterial infection of the endocardium; embolic and renal complications do not consistently meet the involvement threshold.
Inherited ventricular arrhythmia; syncope reflects transient circulatory impairment rather than direct neurologic damage.
Acute metabolic syndrome defined by encephalopathy/cerebral edema, hepatic fatty change and hypoglycemia.
Defining spastic paraplegia and persistent pigment/hair abnormalities; kyphoscoliosis is frequent (30-79%). Bowel dysfunction is neurologic; horseshoe kidney is occasional.
Defining marrow disease, developmental impairment and ocular malformations; hip dysplasia 3/3, osteopenia 2/3. Tracheomalacia 2/3 and hypertriglyceridemia 3/3 omitted by cap.
Peroxisome biogenesis disorder; neurologic dysfunction and cataract/retinal disease affect most classic cases across subtypes. Severe skeletal dysplasia is subtype-dependent.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable sites; no single anatomical organ is established as commonly affected across the group.
